name: Eclipse Mosquitto
summary: An MQTT broker and client toolkit that routes topic-based messages through listener and client session state, with optional persistence and plugin boundaries.

features.name: Broker and client toolkit
features.description: Mosquitto implements MQTT 5.0, 3.1.1, and 3.1 server behavior and also ships a C/C++ client library and command-line publishing and subscribing tools.
benefits: Provides compatible broker and client integration surfaces
Supports both embedded library users and command-line workflows
costs: Protocol version and client capability differences remain interoperability concerns
A broker deployment has different operational requirements from a client library

features.name: Listener and client-session boundaries
features.description: The broker source represents configured listeners and accepted client contexts separately, with connection, packet, subscription, authentication, and disconnect handlers attached to client lifecycle state.
benefits: Separates network admission from per-client protocol state
Provides clear lifecycle hooks for authentication, subscriptions, and disconnect handling
costs: Listener configuration and client state must remain consistent under reload and failure
Per-client state consumes broker memory and scheduling resources

features.name: Topic-routed message queue
features.description: Mosquitto stores broker messages and queues outgoing and incoming client messages around topic publish, subscribe, retain, expiry, QoS, and in-flight state operations.
benefits: Decouples publication from delivery to each subscribed client
Makes expiry, QoS, retained messages, and in-flight work explicit state
costs: Queue memory and delivery behavior depend on client connectivity and QoS
Expiry and retry state complicate the otherwise simple publish path

features.name: Event-driven broker loop
features.description: The broker main loop repeatedly performs expiry, queued-plugin message, client cleanup, keepalive, session, bridge, and plugin work before dispatching multiplexed network activity.
benefits: Combines network readiness with periodic protocol and maintenance work
Allows many client sessions to share a broker process
costs: A slow handler or overloaded queue can affect other sessions
Timer, socket, and protocol state interact in one scheduling boundary

features.name: Optional SQLite-backed broker persistence
features.description: The official build documentation identifies SQLite as an optional dependency for broker persistence, so deployments can compile persistence support separately from the core broker loop.
benefits: Allows deployments to choose a persistence footprint
Separates durable session/message state from transient broker execution
costs: Non-persistent builds have different restart and delivery behavior
Durability introduces database configuration and I/O costs

mathematical_views.question: Which client queues receive a published message under the broker's topic and subscription state?
assumptions: Clients and subscriptions are modeled as finite broker state
Topic matching, QoS, retain, and expiry are explicit routing parameters
The view abstracts packet encoding and network timing

mathematical_views.question: How do socket readiness, client protocol events, timers, and queued maintenance work advance broker state?
assumptions: The broker loop is modeled as repeated transitions over shared listener, client, and queue state
Multiplexed I/O and periodic checks are distinct transition causes
The model does not infer fairness or delivery guarantees beyond the protocol and configuration

benefits: A complete protocol ecosystem around MQTT
costs: Broker, client, and protocol-version concerns must be coordinated

benefits: Explicit admission and session lifecycle boundaries

costs: Queue growth, retry, expiry, and QoS state

benefits: Shared process scheduling for network and maintenance work
costs: Handler and queue load can couple session latency
Persistence adds I/O and deployment variability
